newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico designates Nuevo Laredo for nat gas network.
newsitem.headline: Mexico designates Nuevo Laredo for nat gas network.

text.p: Border city Nuevo Laredo, in the northern state of Tamaulipas, will be the next area to sell rights to natural gas distribution, Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission said in Monday's official gazette.
The city and surrounding area will constitute the third site designated by the Mexican government for natural gas distribution rights sale to private companies.
Repsol Mexico has already expressed interest in the Nuevo Laredo concession, according to the publication.
The Nuevo Laredo region had 217,648 residents as of the 1990 census, with a possible population of 317,515 by 2010, officials said. Situated on the border with Texas, it is a thriving industrial hub.
Potential consumption in the region could reach "more than two million kilocalories per day," the commission said.
Gas is supplied to the region via ducts from state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos.
